annotations.title: Check a table of values against cited limits

description: Which results in a lab table are over the limit? A lab table in one call: up to 200 rows of parameter, value and unit, checked against the limits held for one place (and a medium or statistic). Each row is answered by check_value itself: its verdicts (over, within, under, not_comparable with a `why`), `counts` and `says`, or its own coded refusal (an unknown parameter, a value below detection such as <0.005, an ambiguous unit). Each held limit is sent once, in `limits`, and a verdict names it by index: joined, they are check_value's row, with its `cite`. `summary` counts the rows over a limit, under a floor, within every limit, with no comparable limit, and refused by code. `max_rows` pages each row's verdicts (over first); ask check_value with `offset` for more.

max_rows.description: Verdicts returned for each row (its counts cover all).

medium.description: What the limits govern: an effluent (water_discharge), the receiving water (surface_water), groundwater, ...

place.description: ISO 3166 code of where the rule binds: a country (US, CA, DE, FR, IT), a state or province (US-OH, CA-QC), or EU. A place also searches every place above it: US-OH searches US-OH and US; DE searches DE and EU. One place for the whole table.

rows.description: The table's rows, in order; the answer keeps the order.

parameter.description: The substance or measure as a regulation names it (copper, ammonia, pH) or its CAS number.

unit.description: The value's unit: mg/L, µg/L, ng/L, mg/kg, pH ...

value.description: The measured value as the table prints it (0.15, "0,15"); a result below detection ("<0.005") is refused for that row, never compared.

statistic.description: Only limits under this statistic: daily_max, monthly_avg, instant, ...

name: check_values
title: Check a table of values against cited limits
